ella_cs: Hey team — AcroLabs onboarding. They're seeing 429s from our API when their Lambda warmup (concurrent cold starts) fires. Node SDK v0.8.3, they call initialize() in a handler and then immediately fan out requests. They say it happens only during the first 20s after deploy. Any quick playbook?

raj_engineer: Do we have logs from their account id? ask for the request IDs. 429 pattern usually preflight/auth fanout or ephemeral token stampede.

ella_cs: Pasted logs from customer (redacted):

```
2024-06-14T15:02:12Z INFO request_id=abc123 POST /v1/generate 200
2024-06-14T15:02:13Z INFO request_id=abc124 POST /v1/generate 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
2024-06-14T15:02:13Z INFO request_id=abc125 POST /v1/generate 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
```

sam_platform: Looks like a classic warmup fanout. Lambdas spawn many containers and each one calls token refresh simultaneously. Which auth mode are they using? Ephemeral JWTs via our SDK?

ella_cs: Yes ephemeral tokens via their central auth service. They do a preflight on cold start to fetch key, then spawn 10 concurrent handlers.

raj_engineer: Two quick mitigations: 1) Suggest client-side prefetch + single token share across warmup attempts (SDK has ephemeralTokenCache option). 2) Add a tiny randomized jitter on handler init so not all instances refresh at the same ms. Example: 

```
const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*250);
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, jitter));
await RedwoodSDK.initialize({ ephemeralTokenCache: true });
```

maria_ops: Also recommend lowering prefetch concurrency in their bootstrap (we expose PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY env). If they set PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 during warmup it serializes refreshes.

ella_cs: I told them to try both. They asked if we can change server-side to be more tolerant for short windows.

raj_engineer: We can add a short grace for ephemeral token creation during onboarding ramps (token creation queue). But that's a prod change; for immediate relief do client-side.

infra-bot: Deploy bot: Canary rollout of ephemeral-token-backoff v2 scheduled for 2024-06-15 03:00 UTC.

sam_platform: Another trick: have the Lambda reuse a small in-memory token cache that's warmed by a managed init function (once-per-container). That prevents cross-instance fanout. Also check their SDK version; older v0.8.3 had a bug where concurrent init didn't respect backoff — they should try v0.9.x.

ella_cs: Customer tried jitter + PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 and saw immediate drop in 429s. They want a short note to include in their runbook. Can someone paste a 1-paragraph recommendation?

raj_engineer: Quick runbook blurb: "During serverless warmup, avoid simultaneous ephemeral token refreshes from multiple cold-started instances. Recommended pattern: upgrade to SDK v0.9+, enable ephemeralTokenCache (shared per-container), set PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 for initial startup bursts, and add a small randomized init jitter (0-250ms). These steps serialize token refreshes and reduce short-window 429s without changing server-side quotas." :thumbsup:

ella_cs: Perfect — passed to customer, they marked as mitigated. I'll follow up next week about upgrading. Thanks all.

maria_ops: Filing a small docs note for serverless warmup patterns in the onboarding playbook.

sam_platform: FYI I'll open a ticket to track SDK v0.8.3 concurrent-init backoff bug so we can nudge customers during onboarding.

ella_cs: Closing this thread in CS notes.
